chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not prescribe for women any making up (of missed fasts) nor any fasting other than the fasting of Ramadan, except if it is a vow, or fasting for expiation, or voluntary fasting.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on women making up missed fasts in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this ruling to clarify the distinction between obligatory (Fard) and voluntary (Tatawwu') fasting for women, emphasizing that menstruation and postpartum bleeding exempt them from making up missed days, unlike other obligations. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the exemption is rooted in the Quranic concession for those unable to fast, distinguishing it from vows or expiations which remain binding regardless of physical state. The hadith serves to prevent unnecessary burden on women by clarifying that missed Ramadan fasts are not required to be made up if the delay is due to valid excuses like menstruation, provided they make them up later.
